text:
The Oilers sit first in the Pacific and are winless in four, and both things are true for the same reason. Edmonton has a +24 goal difference while being slightly outchanced, because its shooters have scored 25.7 more goals than their chances usually produce. The last four games have been honest: outscored 20-12, with 44% of the expected goals (the quality of chances). For Mike Babcock's team, this skid is one the chances say is real.

The stars are still doing star things. Connor McDavid's pace has people, Wayne Gretzky included, talking about a 200-point season, per NHL.com, and Leon Draisaitl just reached 1,100 career points. We have Draisaitl at 51% to score and McDavid at 93% for a point. Devon Levi starts in goal, just under even this season, and Zach Hyman is off the out list and day-to-day. Our Sleeper is Kasperi Kapanen, at 47% for a point with his ice time up.

Seattle lost 3-1 to Chicago on Wednesday and went 0-for-4 on the power play. After the loss in San Jose, Lane Lambert called the penalty kill "the elephant in the room," per Alison Lukan's post. Jared McCann is out until about January, Matty Beniers has moved onto the top power play, and 20-year-old Berkly Catton, who set a franchise mark with his first NHL hat trick, is up to 16:25 a night.

Jordan Eberle comes back to the city where his career started two points from 800, having scored his 100th goal as a Kraken on Wednesday. Our numbers have Edmonton at 3.20 expected goals and Seattle at 2.49. Philipp Grubauer starts for the Kraken, right around even this season. The Oilers beat Seattle 3-1 on Oct. 3, and our playoff odds have the Kraken at 27%, 15 points back of Edmonton in the division.
headline: Struggling Oilers host a Kraken team with questions
